game: DEN @ LAC Week 3 2025, kickoff 2025-09-21 16:05 ET, SoFi dome

script.base: Dome, LAC -2.5, total 45.5, implied LAC 24.0 / DEN 21.5. One-score game with both offenses on schedule: Herbert and Nix throw, Dobbins (30 carries, 139 rush yards in two games) and Hampton (23 carries, 72 yards, 3.13 YPC) both stay involved, and a 2.5 spread is not a garbage-time or clock-kill script. Moderate total, not a shootout and not a slog.
script.flip1: Herbert cooks DEN's 36% blitz (LAC EPA/db +0.60 vs blitz vs +0.34 vs none), LAC leads by 10+ at half, Hampton plus Herbert (already 69 rush yards) salt the clock, Dobbins's carries die, and DEN pass volume spikes to Franklin, Sutton and whoever replaces Engram.
script.flip2: Dobbins hits the explosive-run soft spot LAC has shown (8 runs of 10+, 4.61 YPC), DEN leads late, LAC abandons Hampton, and Herbert has to throw — Johnston/Allen/McConkey volume up, Franklin cools if Denver runs the clock.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report, not inactives: DEN TE Evan Engram OUT (back) after 6 targets / 33 yards / 19 air yards, all short-area. Same-position next man is Adam Trautman (4 targets, 15 yards, 12 air); no Trautman prop is listed. Tyler Badie (8 targets, 35 yards, 8 air, recyds 17.5) can take a checkdown slice, not the full TE share. DEN LB Dre Greenlaw OUT (quad) helps LAC underneath — Allen, McConkey, Hampton and Najee receiving — more than deep shots. LAC TE Will Dissly OUT (knee) is a small vacuum: he has no targets in the two-game log and Tyler Conklin already has the 2 TE targets (50 yards). LAC S Elijah Molden OUT (hamstring) helps DEN deep shots (Sutton 154 air, Franklin 105 air) and partially offsets LAC's strong outside YPA. LAC LB Daiyan Henley Q (illness) and CB Cam Hart Q (hip) are not ruled out; do not treat them as out before inactives. Final inactives are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack (no coverage charting). Known shells: LAC blitzes only 26% and has been gashed in the middle (8.59 YPA on 17) while holding the perimeter (left 4.58 on 36, right 4.54 on 28). DEN blitzes 36% and has been gashed outside (left 7.38 on 32, right 7.14 on 22) while the middle is 4.38 on only 8 attempts.
matchup.pressure: LAC's 26% blitz is the look Nix has handled (DEN EPA/db +0.17 vs no blitz, -0.33 vs blitz), so this is not a sack-and-checkdown script for Denver. DEN's 36% blitz is a gift to Herbert (LAC EPA/db +0.60 vs blitz): pressure has raised Chargers EPA, so it does not kill Johnston's deep shots.
matchup.bleeds: LAC bleeds the middle (8.59 YPA) and explosives (6 passes of 20+ for 86 yards; 8 runs of 10+ at 4.61 YPC). DEN bleeds the perimeter (7.38/7.14 YPA), has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ for 69 yards, and only 3 runs of 10+ at 4.49 YPC. Run explosives are a LAC-defense problem, not a DEN-defense problem.
matchup.overlap: Franklin is DEN's target leader (15 targets, 133 yards, 105 air, 7.0 aDOT) and is the intermediate profile aimed at LAC's middle hole; Sutton (13 targets, 154 air, 11.8 aDOT, only 67 yards) is aimed at the perimeter LAC actually defends, so he is not the overlap. Johnston (14 targets, 150 yards, 202 air, 14.4 aDOT) is the vertical profile aimed at DEN's perimeter hole, with Herbert's blitz EPA behind it. Allen (17 targets, 8.4 aDOT, 129 yards) is the volume king but less specifically that bleed. Alignment is inferred from air yards, not charted.

form: Only weeks 1-2, so no 3-4 game trend and no similar-defense sample in the pack. Franklin 44 then 89 (mean equals the 66.5 line). Sutton 61 then 6, air yards not converting. Dobbins rush 63 then 76 on 30 carries, stable role; Harvey 70 then 8, unstable. Johnston 79 then 71, both near 75.5, the most stable high producer. Allen 68 then 61. McConkey 74 then 48. Hampton 48 then 24 at 3.13 YPC, with Herbert also rushing for 69. Najee 5 then 28. Badie receiving 16 then 19. Mims 12 then 24. No OC or QB change is noted in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. Franklin was the outside X, not the middle, so he ran into LAC's 4.54-4.58 YPA perimeter, Hart played, and the 44-yard week was the real role — he finished in the 40s while Trautman and Badie took Engram's short middle work and Sutton's one explosive was Denver's only chunk. Johnston's 14.4 aDOT ran into a DEN defense that has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ (69 yards); the 7.3 outside YPA was intermediate YAC, not bombs, Greenlaw's absence fed Allen and McConkey underneath, and a 71-yard game repeated. The close script also tilted run, Dobbins and Hampton drained plays, and 66.5 plus 75.5 was too many yards out of a 45.5 total once the explosives missed. No saved price means the number we would have laid is unknown.
slip_story: One story: competitive dome pass game, not a clock-kill and not a weather under. Franklin over (DEN attacks LAC's middle, low blitz) with Johnston over (LAC attacks DEN's perimeter on a blitz Herbert has crushed). Both live in the base one-score script. Do not add Dobbins or Hampton overs — those need the lead-and-run flip these WRs do not. Do not add a total under. No TDs, one market per player, two legs. Sutton under is the trap side (high aDOT into a 4.5 YPA perimeter) but Molden out conflicts, so he stays off the slip. Badie over 17.5 is the Engram sleeper and is not forced, because Trautman is the same-position replacement and has no prop.
